newsitem.title: UK: UK government loses majority on finance bill cttee.
newsitem.headline: UK government loses majority on finance bill cttee.

text.p: The British government has agreed that it should no longer have a majority on the parliamentary committee scrutinising the Finance Bill which implements last November's budget, a parliamentary official confirmed on Thursday.

The concession, a recognition that the government has lost its overall majority in the House of Commons, means it will be more difficult for the government to carry any "tidying up" amendments it may wish to put forward.
But a Treasury spokesman said: "The government is still confident of getting its bill through in good time and in good order."
A list of 32 members of the committee appeared on Thursday's parliamentary order paper consisting of 17 Conservatives and 15 Labour members.
However the official of parliament's selection committee said that, due to an oversight, the names of two Liberal Democrats who will sit on the committee had been omitted.
By convention, a Conservative will chair the committee. He or she will be bound in the case of tied votes to break the deadlock by declaring for the status quo.
This means that the Conservatives, provided they all attend, should be able to frustrate any opposition attempts to amend the bill.
But the government frequently finds it needs to amend its own legislation because it discovers loopholes in the original drafting.

In theory the opposition could prevent any such amendments going through, although in practice it would be unlikely to do so if the amendments were on technical matters which clearly needed to be addressed. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
